passages.text: Nevertheless, although the origin was one, many divisions of kingship arose in this way. The Persians were the first to take coals from the lightning bolt that fell from heaven and keep them alive with fuel of their own. They accorded the fire special honor as a heavenly god; and because they were the first to worship it, they were the first to be honored with kingship by that very fire. After them, the Babylonians stole coals from the fire there, carried them safely into their own lands, and worshiped it; consequently, they too reigned next. The Egyptians acted likewise and in their own language called the fire Phthae, which is interpreted “Hephaestus”; the first to reign among them is also designated by his name. Those who reigned in each locality, then, adopted this same practice, made an image, and kindled altars in honor of the fire. Most of them were extinguished from kingship;

lexical_decisions.chosen: although the origin was one
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπαρχή can denote an origin, beginning, or underlying basis; “origin” fits the ensuing account of how multiple kingdoms arose from one practice.

lexical_decisions.chosen: keep them alive with fuel of their own
lexical_decisions.rationale: τροφή literally denotes nourishment; for coals, “fuel” conveys the image of sustaining or feeding the fire.

lexical_decisions.chosen: into their own lands
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized neuter plural is elliptical and may mean their own places, territory, or possessions; “lands” fits the movement of the coals from Persia to Babylonia.

lexical_decisions.chosen: called the fire Phthae, which is interpreted “Hephaestus”
lexical_decisions.rationale: The Egyptian name is retained in transliteration, while ἑρμηνεύεται introduces the Greek identification supplied by the author.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς μὲν βασιλείας οἱ πλεῖστοι ἀπεσβέσθησαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Most of them were extinguished from kingship
lexical_decisions.rationale: The marked “extinguished” metaphor is preserved because it echoes the preceding fire imagery; smoother alternatives such as “lost their kingdoms” would erase that wordplay.

passages.text: Yet they did not cease reverencing the carved images, because of the wicked contrivance of the Magi, who found pretexts for them capable of holding them fast to futile worship. After installing the images with magical rites, they appointed festivals for them consisting of sacrifices, libations, flutes, and clapping. Deceived under cover of these things, the senseless—even though their kingship had been taken away—do not abandon the accumulated religious observances. To such an extent, because of their love of pleasure, have they preferred error to truth. They also, after becoming drunk, raise a ritual cry beside the altar, while their soul, from its depths as if through dreams, foretells to them the punishment that is to come for such deeds of theirs.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the wicked contrivance of the Magi
lexical_decisions.rationale: μάγοι may denote Magi or magicians; “Magi” preserves the historically specific designation while the surrounding magical rites clarify the polemical sense.

lexical_decisions.chosen: After installing the images with magical rites
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἱδρύω can mean set up, install, or consecrate an image; “installing” preserves the physical and ritual dimensions without asserting a formal consecration not explicitly stated.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ τε θυμάτων, σπονδῶν, αὐλῶν τε καὶ κρότων
lexical_decisions.chosen: consisting of sacrifices, libations, flutes, and clapping
lexical_decisions.rationale: κρότοι can refer to clapping, striking sounds, or noisy applause; “clapping” gives a concrete counterpart to the flutes while retaining the festival setting.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the accumulated religious observances
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally, these are observances that have “come together.” “Accumulated” reflects their combination in the festivals; “combined observances” or “religious gatherings” are also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: raise a ritual cry beside the altar
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὀλολύζω denotes a loud ritual cry or ululation, and παραβώμιον locates it beside the altar.

passages.text: Though many forms of worship have passed through the world, and a form of worship has been handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, we—the good merchants—are here bringing it to you like a pearl, displaying it and placing it before your judgment and within your authority. Choose what seems right to you. If, then, you choose what is ours, you will be able not only to escape demons and sufferings caused by demons, but also, as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them, you will enjoy the good things that will exist forever.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολλῶν οὖν ἐν βίῳ παρελθουσῶν θρησκειῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Though many forms of worship have passed through the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: θρησκεῖαι are forms of worship or religious observances, while ἐν βίῳ may mean in life or in the world; “passed through the world” avoids asserting that all have ceased to exist.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ προγόνων ἡμῖν παραδοθείσης καὶ φυλαχθείσης θρησκείας ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην
lexical_decisions.chosen: a form of worship has been handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved ... bringing it to you like a pearl
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive phrase is read as a circumstantial construction whose worship is the understood object represented as a pearl. It can alternatively be construed more compactly as “a pearl, as it were, of the worship handed down.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: we—the good merchants
lexical_decisions.rationale: The nominative phrase is appositional to the implied subject of πάρεσμεν and sustains the pearl-trading image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπὶ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ κρίσει καὶ ἐξουσίᾳ τιθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: placing it before your judgment and within your authority
lexical_decisions.rationale: κρίσις denotes judgment or evaluation, while ἐξουσία denotes authority, freedom of action, or disposal; the rendering preserves both aspects of the hearers’ choice.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you choose what is ours
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter plural leaves the referent implicit and may encompass the speakers’ teaching, worship, and practices; the English retains that breadth.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτοὶ αὐτὰ φυγαδεύοντες καὶ ἱκετευόμενοι ὑπ’ αὐτῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first pronoun may collect the demons and demonic sufferings, while the agent of the imploring is most naturally the demons. The English preserves the source pronouns rather than narrowing the first referent.

passages.text: For otherwise, while in the present life you are abused by demons with strange afflictions, upon release from the body you will also have your souls facing punishment forever—in truth, not because God condemns them, but because evil deeds carry such a judgment. For the demons, having authority through the food rendered to them, are admitted by your own hands into your bodies. After dwelling deep within for a long time, they become blended with the soul. And because of the negligence of those who do not understand how to help themselves, or who are even unwilling, the soul of these very people, being united to the demon when the body is dissolved, must be carried by it to whatever places it wishes. Worst of all, when, at the consummation of all things, the demon is first handed over to the purifying fire, the soul blended with it must itself be punished indescribably, while the demon takes pleasure. For the soul, since it comes from light, cannot bear the flame of the fire, which is foreign to its kind, and is tormented; but the demon, being within the substance of its own kind, takes immense pleasure, having become an unbreakable bond for the soul that, under its power, suffers with it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you are abused by demons with strange afflictions
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνυβρίζω conveys abusive or outrageous treatment, and ἀλλόκοτος denotes what is strange, alien, or extraordinary.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ ἀληθῆ οὐ θεοῦ καταδικάζοντος, ἀλλὰ κακῶν πράξεων τοιαύτην ἐχουσῶν κρίσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: in truth, not because God condemns them, but because evil deeds carry such a judgment
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ ἀληθῆ functions adverbially as “in truth.” The following genitive constructions contrast divine condemnation with the judgment inherent in evil deeds; the unstated object of καταδικάζοντος is supplied from the souls just mentioned.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through the food rendered to them
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀποδίδω can mean give back, render, or deliver what is due; “rendered” preserves the suggestion of food offered to demons rather than ordinary eating alone.

lexical_decisions.chosen: After dwelling deep within for a long time
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνδομυχέω describes entering or lodging in the innermost recesses; “dwelling deep within” preserves the spatial image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: be punished indescribably
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπορρήτως can mean unspeakably or in a manner that cannot be disclosed; “indescribably” fits the intensity of punishment without suggesting that it is merely secret.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the flame of the fire, which is foreign to its kind
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀλλόφυλος literally means belonging to another race or kind. The flame is foreign to the soul that comes from light, not foreign to the demon whose substance is said to share its kind.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δεσμὸς δύσρηκτος γενόμενος τῆς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ συμπαθείσης ψυχῆς
lexical_decisions.chosen: having become an unbreakable bond for the soul that, under its power, suffers with it
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ may express the demon’s agency or controlling power, while συμπαθείσης depicts the soul suffering together with it. “The soul made by it to suffer together” is a possible more explicitly causal rendering.

source_issues.source_quote: οἱ γὰρ δαίμονες, διὰ τῆς αὐτοῖς ἀποδοθείσης τροφῆς ἐξουσίαν ἔχοντες, ὑπὸ τῶν ὑμετέρων χειρῶν εἰς τὰ ὑμέτερα εἰσκρίνεται σώματα
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints the singular verb εἰσκρίνεται with the plural subject οἱ δαίμονες and the plural participle ἔχοντες. The surrounding syntax clearly supports a plural sense, so the English normalizes the number while this printed disagreement is disclosed.

passages.text: As for the demons’ eagerness to slip into human bodies, this is the cause. Being spirits and having desire for foods, drinks, and intercourse, yet being unable to partake because they are spirits and need instruments suited to their use, they enter human bodies so that, obtaining them as instruments that serve them, they may be able to obtain what they want—whether foods through the person’s teeth or intercourse through that person’s genitals. Consequently, to put demons to flight, deprivation, fasting, and hardship are the most fitting aid. For if they enter a human body for the sake of partaking, it is clear that hardship drives them out. But since some are more formidable and, having persisted obstinately, remain in the body undergoing punishment even while they themselves are being punished, it is therefore necessary to take refuge in God with prayers and supplications, while abstaining from every occasion of impurity, so that God’s hand may be able to touch that person for healing, as one who is pure and believes.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς δαίμονας γλίχεσθαι εἰς τὰ ἀνθρώπων εἰσδύειν σώματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: the demons’ eagerness to slip into human bodies
lexical_decisions.rationale: γλίχομαι expresses eager desire or striving, while εἰσδύω depicts entering or slipping into something.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς βρωτὰ καὶ ποτὰ καὶ συνουσίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: for foods, drinks, and intercourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: Although συνουσία can denote association generally, the later reference to the genitals establishes sexual intercourse here.

lexical_decisions.chosen: obtaining them as instruments that serve them
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπουργέω describes rendering subordinate service; the human bodies function as instrumental agents through which the demons satisfy their desires.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ ἔνδεια καὶ ἡ νηστεία καὶ ἡ κακουχία
lexical_decisions.chosen: deprivation, fasting, and hardship
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔνδεια denotes lack or deprivation, while κακουχία denotes harsh treatment, bodily hardship, or privation; the separate terms are retained rather than collapsed into fasting.

lexical_decisions.chosen: having persisted obstinately
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound conveys continued contentious resistance or stubborn persistence; “persisted obstinately” fits demons that remain despite punishment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while abstaining from every occasion of impurity
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόφασις can mean pretext, occasion, or ostensible cause. “Occasion” best fits practical abstention, though “every impure pretext” remains possible.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ χεὶρ εἰς ἴασιν αὐτοῦ ἐπιψαῦσαι δυνηθῇ ὡς ἁγνοῦ καὶ πιστεύοντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: God’s hand may be able to touch that person for healing, as one who is pure and believes
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπιψαύω takes the genitive αὐτοῦ. Although the pronoun could grammatically look back toward the body, the accompanying “pure and believing” identifies the intended referent as the afflicted person.
